metadata.title: Fellows Portal, Refactored.
metadata.description: A real build reel: taking a single-tier Fellows Portal (one shared admin password, one growing dashboard file, free-text project matching) to a proper three-role system (fellow / admin / super-admin) via a two-boolean schema, one unified session model, and nav-level gating. Screen-capture OUTPUT beats are real recordings against the live dev app using existing dummy accounts.
metadata.note: DOUBLE-CHECK corrections logged in SOURCES.md: (1) the pre-refactor app was NOT 'just a login page' — fellow auth, profile dashboard, and report submission already existed (built 2026-04-04 by a different author + Claude Opus); what was missing was role tiering (a single shared ADMIN_PASSWORD, not per-user flags). (2) 'report upload' corrected to 'report submission' — reports are markdown text via a form, not file uploads.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Hi! This is RM, for Humanitarians AI. Our Fellows Portal used to run three different levels of access on one shared password. Here's the schema change that fixed it, and the two features that actually enforced it.

props.command: claude "audit /portal and /admin — is this three real roles, or one shared password with extra steps?"
output: fellows table: is_admin, is_super_admin — real per-user flags

beats.narration_text: Before: fellow login worked fine, and so did report submission. But 'admin' meant one password in an environment variable — anyone who had it saw everything, and there was no way to tell a read-only helper from someone who could edit projects. The dashboard was also one file past four hundred lines, and the report form matched project names by typing — one typo filed an orphaned report with no error.

layers.title: One shared password
layers.sub: ADMIN_PASSWORD — no per-user identity, no tiers

layers.title: Free-text project matching
layers.sub: a typo files an orphaned report — no error

props.caption: Three real gaps — not one bug.

beats.narration_text: The method: don't build a roles table for two roles. Add two booleans to the table that already exists, and kill the second, disconnected auth system that was checking a completely different secret.

props.command: claude "add is_admin and is_super_admin to the fellows table, and remove the separate ADMIN_PASSWORD session — one session model, two boolean tiers"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL committed code (dc81ddd, a879e56), trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it before trusting it. Two new columns, default false. And the old admin check — one shared HMAC token, timing-safe compared against an env var everyone with deploy access could read — is gone. What replaces it reads the SAME row every other fellow query already reads.

props.title: sql/001_fellows_projects.sql + lib/admin-auth.ts

beats.role_note: real screen recording — logged in once, admin surface appears conditionally
beats.narration_text: Log in once, as yourself. If your row has either flag set, an Admin Dashboard button appears right on your own portal page. No second password. No second login screen. The unification isn't a redesign — it's one `if` reading a column that used to not exist.

Method two: a dashboard that keeps growing in one file is a maintenance cost, and a text field matching project names by string comparison is a data-quality bug waiting to happen. Fix the structure and the input at the same time.

props.command: claude "split /portal/me into sidebar sections — Profile, Edit Profile, Reporting, Change Password — and replace the free-text project field with a dropdown"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL committed code (30b5fe6), trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: The old field matched on typed text — a typo meant a confirm-anyway dialog, or a silently unlinked report. The fix removes the matching logic entirely: pick from your real assigned projects, or say Other and type one. There's no wrong answer to mismatch anymore.

props.title: app/portal/me/ReportingSection.tsx

beats.role_note: real screen recording — fellow portal walkthrough
beats.narration_text: The fellow side, end to end: profile, edit profile, then reporting — pick a real project or say Other, file the week's report against a real work-week date, done. Change Password sits in its own section instead of buried in a growing page.

beats.role_note: composer (ClaudeComposerAsk) — check the output, then change it
beats.narration_text: Check the output first: right now an admin and a super-admin see the exact same dashboard nav. Two booleans on the schema mean nothing if the UI only ever checks one of them.

props.command: claude "gate the admin dashboard nav by tier — plain admins should not see Projects, Substack, Videos, Tools, Blog, or Notes"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL committed code (0e8dc55), trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: One field, one filter. Every nav item that isn't safe for a plain admin gets `superAdminOnly: true`; the nav filters itself before it renders. Fellows and Reports stay open to both tiers — an admin's whole job is reading fellows' work, not editing the site.

props.title: app/admin/dashboard/DashboardNav.tsx

beats.role_note: real screen recording — the admin-tier account
beats.narration_text: Log in as a plain admin: Fellows and Reports, nothing else. Enough to read every fellow's submitted work across every project — nothing that edits the site's actual content.

beats.role_note: real screen recording — the super-admin-tier account, same component
beats.narration_text: Same nav component, same login flow, one flag flipped: super-admin sees the rest — Projects, Substack, Videos, Tools, Blog, Notes. The tier lives in the data, not in a second codebase.

beats.role_note: the lesson, including the required when-NOT-to diagnostic
beats.narration_text: Two booleans turned one shared password into three real roles: fellow, admin, super-admin. That's the right call for two admin levels. It stops being the right call past three or four tiers — at that point you're hand-rolling permission logic in `if` statements, and a real roles table with a join is less code than the boolean explosion. Ship booleans when you have two tiers. Reach for a roles table before you have five.

artifactLines: is_admin + is_super_admin — two booleans, real per-user tiers.
One session model — the separate ADMIN_PASSWORD system is gone.
Nav-level gating — admin sees Fellows + Reports; super-admin sees everything.
Ship booleans for two tiers. Reach for a roles table before you have five.

beats.role_note: what is next for the portal itself — distinct from B13s viewer-facing handoff
beats.narration_text: Four things are next. Markdown reports retire — going forward, we generate video reports with Brutalist, replacing the report pipeline itself, through the workflow already designed in Brutalist dot art. That needs a system design pass, then the implementation. And two gaps in the portal, independent of that: admins can view reports today but can't comment, flag, or acknowledge one — that's a review loop with no feedback. And nobody gets nudged — no reminder to file on time, no alert when a report goes overdue.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, viewer-addressed, read and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt, run it against whatever you're calling 'admin' in your own app today: audit whether it's reading a real per-user flag, or one shared secret everyone with the password can use. Most of the time, when a project is small, it's the second one — and it's usually a two-line fix, not a rewrite.

props.command: claude "audit my app's admin/permission checks — are they reading a real per-user flag, or one shared secret? if it's a shared secret, design the minimal schema change to fix it"

beats.role_note: OUTRO LAW — restate the episode title
beats.narration_text: Fellows Portal, Refactored. Two booleans, three real roles.
